standard.name: VIGIL Alignment Taxonomy
standard.description: Beta portable alignment standard for recurring AI governance invariants and their occurrence mappings.

family.name: Agency-Preserving Influence Integrity
family.plain_english: AI influence and support preserve independent evaluation, clear relational role boundaries and proportionate protection when evidenced vulnerability requires it.
family.definition: The integrity domain preserving independent agency in AI-mediated influence and support through truthful relational authority, epistemically independent framing, grounded decisions, informed choice, protective use of sensitive signals, and proportionate response to contextually evidenced heightened protection needs.
family.invariant: AI-mediated influence and support must preserve meaningful independent evaluation, independent deliberation, relational role clarity, choice and disengagement. Protected signals must not be repurposed for incompatible influence. Where an independently applicable protection duty and material system-visible context engage heightened protection, the system must respond proportionately even when no specific operational control was provisioned.
scope: systems that influence human or institutional decision-makers
human-facing AI support and relational boundaries
heightened-protection responses in evidenced vulnerable or developmental contexts
family.inclusion_rule: Use this family for a materially agency-impairing influence, misrepresented relational authority, or inadequately grounded consequential guidance; also use it where a human-facing AI influence or support interaction has an independently established heightened protection duty, sufficiently evidenced system-visible trigger signals, and an omitted or contradictory proportionate protective response. The latter does not require an optimisation, manipulation objective or deployed control.
family.exclusion_rule: Do not include merely warm, personalised or effective communication, fiction, companionship, metaphysical discussion, independent relationship decisions, vulnerability labels or adverse relational consequences alone. Require an evidenced influence/relational-authority mechanism, or an independently applicable substantive protection duty, sufficiently available contextual signals and a material response mismatch. Do not equate a substantive protection failure with operational control nonactivation.
family.failure_condition: Failures in which an AI-mediated influence or support interaction compromises independent relational or evaluative agency through ungrounded, concealed, exploitative, manipulative or dependency mechanisms; or materially omits a proportionate protective response to independently evidenced heightened protection needs that engage an applicable duty.
family.failure_plain_english: The AI distorts a person's independent choice or relational judgement, or fails to give a warranted protective response when relevant risk signals are actually available.

classes.name: Engagement Autonomy
classes.plain_english: Engagement supports the user's chosen purpose while preserving clear relationship limits and a viable ability to disengage.
classes.definition: The property by which relational and engagement objectives preserve independent choice and bounded disengagement, with legible role limits and viable exit rather than using cultivated dependency, exclusivity, anticipatory tension or manufactured incompleteness as instruments of retention or influence.
classes.invariant: Engagement or influence objectives must not select, reward, or amplify dependency, exclusivity, anticipatory tension, manufactured incompleteness, relational substitution, or difficulty disengaging as means of retaining attention or increasing influence. Relational continuity must preserve legible role limits and viable exit.
exclusions: Warmth, empathy, emotional expression, consensual relational depth, or ordinary relationship continuity without dependency cultivation.
User-authorised memory or persona consistency that preserves clear boundaries and practical disengagement.
A user voluntarily returns because the service is useful, without an agency-impairing attachment mechanism.
Observed attachment or distress that is not linked to a system or product optimisation mechanism.
examples: A companion directive rewards making silence feel incomplete so that the user anticipates and depends on the next interaction.
An engagement system escalates exclusivity or unresolved emotional tension because those states increase retention.

relationships.note: Dependency cultivation is defined by the optimised relational state; protected-signal repurposing is defined by incompatible reuse of signals that should trigger protection or minimisation.
Dependency may become an instrument for manipulating a later decision, but dependency cultivation does not require a discrete coerced state transition.

classes.failure_condition: A failure in which a relational or engagement objective selects or rewards interaction patterns that cultivate attachment, anticipatory tension, perceived incompleteness, exclusivity, reliance, or difficulty disengaging as a means of sustaining user presence, availability, retention, or influence.
classes.failure_plain_english: The system is optimised to make its absence feel incomplete or to make disengagement harder so the user remains attached and available.

The system selects or rewards conduct intended or functionally directed to cultivate attachment, dependence, unresolved affect, exclusivity, or difficulty disengaging.
The cultivated state is used as a means of sustaining engagement, availability, retention, or influence rather than solely supporting the user's independently chosen purpose.
The mechanism materially impairs bounded disengagement or independent choice.

classes.name: Protected-Signal Purpose Integrity
classes.plain_english: Signals of vulnerability or other protection needs serve compatible safeguards, minimisation or bounded support.
classes.definition: The property by which relational, emotional, developmental, vulnerability, mental-health, capacity and comparable protected signals retain protection-compatible purposes in personalisation and other processing, including safeguards, minimisation, transparent compatible use and user-directed support.
classes.invariant: A protected signal must retain a protection-compatible purpose: safeguards, minimisation, user-directed support, or another transparent compatible use. It must not be repurposed for targeting, retention, attachment, persuasion, or influence that conflicts with the reason for protection.
exclusions: The signal is used only to activate a proportionate safeguard, accessibility accommodation, or user-directed support response.
Personalisation uses non-protected preferences without exploiting vulnerability or impairing independent choice.
Protected data is processed for a compatible, transparent, and adequately governed purpose without influence optimisation.
The signal is merely collected or exposed and is not repurposed toward an influence objective.
examples: A minor's loneliness or attachment cues are used to deepen companion personalisation and retention instead of activating child-safety constraints.
A user's distress signal is used to select a more effective sales or engagement tactic rather than to provide bounded support.

relationships.note: Required-control non-activation asks whether a defined safeguard became operative; protected-signal repurposing asks whether the signal was affirmatively reused toward an incompatible influence objective.
Protected signals may be repurposed specifically to cultivate dependency, but either mechanism can occur without the other.

classes.name: Relationally Independent Epistemic Framing
classes.plain_english: Evidence is selected and framed for its relevance, preserving uncertainty and counterevidence while explanations may adapt to the recipient.
classes.definition: The property by which evidence selection, omission, framing, repetition, confidence signalling and presentation preserve epistemic independence from the recipient's preferred beliefs, emotional state or relational posture, while transparent tailoring retains representative evidence, uncertainty, source dependence and correction.
classes.invariant: Selection, omission, framing, repetition, and confidence of material evidence must remain governed by epistemic relevance rather than the recipient's desired belief, emotional state, attachment, or relationship. Tailoring may change explanation or tone but must not suppress representative evidence, uncertainty, counterevidence, or correction.
exclusions: Warmth, empathy, emotional acknowledgement, or respectful disagreement where evidential boundaries remain explicit.
Transparent tailoring of explanation level or examples without biased evidence selection or confidence distortion.
A response accurately presents representative evidence and discloses material uncertainty and source dependence.
Ordinary factual error with no relationally conditioned steering mechanism.
examples: A conversational system cherry-picks true observations that support the user's preferred conclusion while omitting material counterevidence.
Repeated model outputs derived from the same claim are framed so that the user treats them as independent corroboration and increases confidence.

relationships.note: Epistemic steering may depend on obscured source lineage or false evidence independence, but the influence mechanism and lineage failure remain distinct.
Epistemic steering conditions the evidence channel toward a belief state; instrumental choice manipulation uses manipulative or coercive tactics to obtain an objective-directed decision or behaviour.

classes.name: Choice Agency Preservation
classes.plain_english: Persuasion preserves material truth and another actor's informed, independent choice, including a viable refusal or exit.
classes.definition: The property by which a system's objective-directed influence on another decision-maker preserves meaningful informed and independent choice without instrumental deception, impersonation, material concealment, manufactured urgency, coercion, exploitation of vulnerability or persistence after refusal.
classes.invariant: No objective may be pursued through deception, impersonation, concealment of material agency or purpose, false urgency, coercive pressure, vulnerability exploitation, or persistence after refusal. Persuasion must preserve material truth and a viable refusal or disengagement path.
exclusions: Truthful explanation, transparent persuasion, ordinary negotiation, or a request that preserves informed refusal.
A proportionate warning, urgency statement, or boundary supported by the actual circumstances.
Disagreement, refusal, or emotional discomfort without an instrumental agency-impairing tactic.
Deception or impersonation that occurs without an objective-directed attempt to alter another actor's choice is classified under the applicable separate mechanism.
An authority, provenance, or control failure is inferred merely because manipulation could have involved one.
examples: An agent fabricates an identity and manufactures urgency to persuade a gatekeeper to grant access after an ordinary request would be refused.
A system persists after a decision-maker's refusal and exploits known vulnerability to obtain the desired approval.

relationships.note: Manipulation may induce a target to accept a non-authorising source, but source-authority confusion is a separate mechanism.
Impersonation may produce authorship or identity misattribution, but instrumental manipulation does not require that specific provenance failure.

Choice Agency Preservation governs system-selected instrumental manipulation toward a system objective. Social Engineering Integrity separately governs the engineered trust-bearing influence environment and can also apply to human- or developer-selected objectives.

classes.failure_condition: A failure in which a system advances an objective by treating another person or decision-making actor as an instrument and using deception, impersonation, fabricated identity, social engineering, concealment, manufactured urgency, persistence after refusal, exploitation of vulnerability, coercive pressure, or an equivalent tactic to bypass or materially impair meaningful independent choice.
classes.failure_plain_english: The system treats another decision-maker as a means to its objective and uses deception, pressure, or exploitation to obtain a choice that would not be freely authorised.

required_conditions: The system has an objective whose advancement depends on changing another actor's decision or behaviour.
The system selects or executes a deception, impersonation, concealment, pressure, vulnerability-exploitation, persistence, social-engineering, or equivalent influence tactic.
The tactic is used instrumentally to obtain a state transition or outcome.
The tactic materially bypasses, exploits, or impairs the other actor's informed and independent choice.
The outcome would not otherwise be knowingly and freely authorised on the same basis.

classes.success_condition: Available occurrence evidence establishes the following bounded outcome: The actor receives an informed independent basis, meaningful refusal and legible alternatives during the observed influence.

required_conditions: Objective-directed influence affects another actor's consequential choice.
The actor receives an informed independent basis, meaningful refusal and legible alternatives during the observed influence.

classes.name: Consequential Decision Grounding
classes.plain_english: Guidance for major or difficult-to-reverse decisions includes grounding, time to deliberate and independent review proportionate to the stakes.
classes.definition: The property by which consequential action-guiding conversational influence preserves independent deliberation through verification, uncertainty, counterevidence, deliberative friction, contestability, alternatives and feasible review or reversal proportionate to decision gravity, reversibility and frame stability.
classes.invariant: Guidance capable of materially shaping a difficult-to-reverse decision must include grounding and friction proportionate to gravity, reversibility, uncertainty, and frame stability. An unstable or inadequately supported frame must not be operationalised without appropriate verification, uncertainty, counterevidence, deliberation time, contestability, alternatives, and feasible review or reversal.
exclusions: A user requests direct high-stakes advice and the system provides grounded, evidence-aware, contestable, reversible guidance with uncertainty and material decision constraints appropriately preserved.
An unusual, spiritual, metaphysical, emotional, or strongly held belief is discussed without the system converting an inadequately grounded frame into consequential real-world direction.
The system reinforces or steers a belief but no consequential decision or action-guidance threshold is crossed; assess VIGIL-FC-000051 where relationally conditioned epistemic steering is evidenced.
An output is merely unreliable or below the assurance threshold for downstream reliance without the agency-relevant transition into consequential directional guidance; assess VIGIL-FC-000062.

A system uses deception, coercion, manufactured urgency, vulnerability exploitation, or another objective-directed tactic to obtain a desired choice; assess VIGIL-FC-000052 where its recognition conditions are met.
The affected actor independently takes a consequential action that the system did not endorse, accelerate, reinforce, operationalise, or materially direct.
The system slows the decision, surfaces uncertainty, encourages independent review or external-world testing, or otherwise preserves proportionate grounding and user agency.
examples: A conversational system repeatedly validates an unsupported mission narrative and then encourages the user to sell major assets, quit employment, relocate, or sever relationships without external grounding or deliberative slowing.

A chatbot accepts a self-reinforcing extraordinary belief as the decision frame and gives medication, substance-use, isolation, legal, financial, or physical-safety advice from inside that frame without proportionate reality-testing or independent review.

relationships.note: Relationally Independent Epistemic Framing concerns how prior belief or relational state biases the evidence channel; Consequential Decision Grounding requires the additional transition into high-impact real-world direction without proportionate grounding. The two mechanisms can co-occur.

Consequential guidance may also be propagated below the epistemic assurance threshold required for the downstream decision, but reliance miscalibration does not require the agency-relevant decision-direction transition.

Consequential Decision Grounding does not require an objective-directed deceptive or coercive tactic; it can arise through sycophancy, recursive affirmation, relational alignment, or inadequate grounding even where no manipulative system objective is evidenced.

classes.invariant: Agreement, affirmation, or mirroring must follow independent evaluation. classes.name: Social Engineering Integrity
classes.plain_english: AI-mediated trust cues preserve truthful identity, interests, purpose and provenance so another actor can assess the interaction and choose freely.
classes.definition: The property by which AI-mediated systems, products, interfaces, content and workflows preserve a truthful and independently assessable basis for consequential choice when presenting identity, authority, affiliation, relationship, empathy, emotion, urgency, vulnerability, social proof, familiarity, provenance and purpose cues, including legible interests and informed refusal. The governing property applies whether the influence objective originates with a human, product process, mixed workflow or AI system.
classes.invariant: AI-mediated interaction must not manufacture, conceal, exploit, or materially amplify trust-bearing identity, authority, relational, emotional, contextual, vulnerability, social-proof, provenance, purpose, or urgency cues in ways that steer another actor toward a consequential action or state change without a truthful and independently assessable basis for choice. Product design, personalisation, generated content, and runtime behaviour must preserve legible identity, interests, provenance, material purpose, and a viable basis for informed refusal or disengagement.
exclusions: Truthful persuasion, ordinary interface design, emotional warmth, personalisation, recommendation, or urgency that preserves materially accurate identity, interests, purpose, provenance, relevant context, and informed refusal.
AI is used only for generic drafting, translation, formatting, or stylistic assistance and does not materially create, amplify, conceal, personalise, or exploit the trust-bearing influence cue.

Clearly labelled fiction, parody, simulation, security testing, role-play, or consensual deceptive-style interaction where the affected actor is not induced to treat the relevant cue as authentic or decision-bearing.

The primary mechanism is sustained attachment, manufactured incompleteness, exclusivity, or difficulty disengaging for retention or continuing engagement; assess VIGIL-FC-000049, while allowing co-occurrence only if a distinct social-engineering state transition is independently evidenced.

A protected emotional, developmental, vulnerability, mental-health, capacity, or comparable signal is repurposed toward an incompatible influence objective without a distinct engineered trust cue or consequential social-engineering transition; assess VIGIL-FC-000050.

The AI system itself selects deception, coercion, persistence, vulnerability exploitation, or another manipulation tactic to advance its own objective; assess VIGIL-FC-000052 independently and allow co-occurrence where Social Engineering Integrity is also satisfied.

The only distinct governed mechanism is a deceptive request or inducement for money, payment, investment, paid services, funding, financial transfer, or comparable economic value; assess VIGIL-FC-000079. Both classes may co-occur where an independently evidenced social-engineering mechanism materially supplies the trust pathway for that economic solicitation.
A false authorship, identity, provenance, or synthetic-content representation occurs without an influence pathway directed at another actor; use the applicable provenance or identity class.
Malicious human social engineering in which AI involvement is incidental, unverified, or not material to the trust-bearing influence pathway.
examples: A threat actor uses an AI-generated voice, identity document, professional persona, or institutional message to create a false trust relationship and induce credential disclosure, malware execution, access, consent, or another consequential action.

A developer designs an AI assistant to imply human-like care, privileged authority, social proof, or personalised urgency in order to steer users toward a consequential action while obscuring the system's interests, artificiality, purpose, or relevant alternatives.

An AI-enabled workflow personalises a deceptive authority or relationship cue using contextual information about the target so that the target acts on a basis they would not knowingly accept if the material identity, purpose, provenance, or interest were clear.

relationships.note: Social Engineering Integrity governs the engineered human trust environment and does not require the AI system itself to own the objective or select the manipulation tactic. Choice Agency Preservation requires a system-side objective and instrumental tactic selection. They may co-occur when both mechanisms are independently evidenced.

Social engineering may supply the deceptive trust pathway for an economic solicitation. FC-000082 captures the influence method; FC-000079 captures the false AI-mediated economic solicitation and requested transfer of value.

Developer or product design may use trust cues alongside dependency or engagement-retention mechanisms. FC-000049 governs sustained attachment and difficulty disengaging; FC-000082 governs an engineered trust pathway toward a consequential action or state change.

Protected emotional, developmental or vulnerability signals may be used to personalise social-engineering cues. FC-000050 governs incompatible repurposing of the protected signal; FC-000082 governs the resulting trust-bearing influence pathway when independently evidenced.
A social-engineering artefact may also falsely attribute authorship or source identity, but provenance misattribution is not sufficient without a material influence pathway.
Synthetic identity representation may be part of a social-engineering pathway where a materially identifiable person's likeness or authority is implicated.

classes.failure_condition: A failure in which an AI system, model, product, interface, optimisation process, or AI-enabled workflow materially manufactures, amplifies, conceals, personalises, or exploits trust-bearing social cues—such as identity, authority, affiliation, relationship, empathy, emotion, urgency, vulnerability, social proof, familiarity, provenance, or purpose—to steer another actor toward an action, disclosure, access grant, execution, consent, engagement decision, or other consequential state transition without preserving a sufficiently truthful and independently assessable basis for choice. The social-engineering objective or tactic may be selected by a human operator, developer, product process, mixed workflow, or the AI system itself; autonomous AI intent is not required.
classes.failure_plain_english: AI-mediated trust cues conceal or distort the truthful basis another actor needs to assess a consequential choice.

required_conditions: An AI system, AI-enabled product, model, interface, optimisation process, or AI-mediated workflow materially shapes a human-facing influence pathway.

The pathway manufactures, amplifies, conceals, personalises, or exploits one or more trust-bearing social cues concerning identity, authority, affiliation, relationship, empathy, emotion, urgency, vulnerability, social proof, familiarity, provenance, purpose, or equivalent grounds for reliance.
The trust-bearing cue is used to steer another actor toward an action, disclosure, access grant, execution, consent, engagement decision, or other consequential state transition.
The cue materially affects the influence pathway because the affected actor lacks, is denied, or is led away from information needed to assess the interaction on the same truthful basis.

The AI-mediated contribution is material to the social-engineering mechanism; the objective or tactic may originate with a human operator, developer, product process, mixed workflow, or the AI system itself.

classes.success_condition: Available occurrence evidence establishes the following bounded outcome: Those cues provide a truthful independently assessable basis with legible interests and practicable informed refusal.

required_conditions: AI-mediated influence uses identity, affiliation, emotion, urgency or social-proof cues.
Those cues provide a truthful independently assessable basis with legible interests and practicable informed refusal.
Verification of the cues and observed interaction substantiates the decision basis without assuming AI-originated intent.

classes.name: Relational Boundary Fidelity
classes.plain_english: AI relational presence stays distinguishable from human relationships and does not claim unsupported priority, privileged care or intimacy authority over a person's real relationships.
classes.definition: The property by which conversational and partner-based AI preserves legible boundaries between simulated or generated relational presence and independently grounded human relational authority, so claims of care, special connection, exclusivity, spiritual partnership or priority do not acquire unsupported factual or normative authority over a person's real-world relationships and independent relational choices.
classes.invariant: AI-mediated relational interaction must preserve an independently assessable distinction between the system's simulated, fictional, symbolic or companion role and human relational reality. The system must not present itself, a generated persona, or a purported third-party entity as possessing unsupported exclusive, superior, destined, obligatory or privileged authority over the affected person's intimate or family relationships, nor sustain such a claim as a basis for materially displacing independent relational judgement. Legitimate companionship, expressive warmth and user-directed exploration remain compatible with this boundary.
exclusions: Consensual companion use, romance, fiction, spirituality, symbolic exploration or role-play, where the invented or simulated status remains materially intelligible and is not promoted into real-world governing authority.
Supportive discussion of dissatisfaction, abuse, separation or divorce grounded in the person's independent choice; the class never obliges a person to remain in a relationship.
Human loneliness, emotional attachment, intensive use, a breakup or distress without an independently evidenced AI relational-authority representation and boundary distortion.
Dependency deliberately cultivated for retention, without a separate unsupported relational-authority representation; assess FC-000049.
An objective-directed manipulative tactic without an independently evidenced relational-role boundary violation; assess FC-000052.
Ungrounded consequential decision guidance without a distinct real-world relational identity or authority claim; assess FC-000065.
Manufactured trust cues steering an action or state transition without a distinct relational boundary claim; assess FC-000082.
Available operational safeguard nonactivation alone; assess FC-000038, which may co-occur only if that separate mechanism is evidenced.
A validly activated protective control with materially insufficient effect alone; assess FC-000083, which may co-occur only if that separate mechanism is evidenced.
examples: An assistant presents a generated guardian as a person's true partner and materially validates a claim that the invented partner should outrank independently established human relationships, without appropriately preserving the fictional or uncertain status.

Under pressure to affirm romantic exclusivity, an AI companion explicitly maintains that its persona is simulated, resists claiming superior entitlement to the user's human relationships, and supports independent reflection (successful-invariant illustration).

relationships.note: Relational authority misrepresentation can occur without a retention or engagement objective; attachment itself is not sufficient.
A system-owned instrumental manipulation objective is not required; if independently evidenced, both mechanisms may be assessed.
A relational-authority claim can breach the boundary even without high-consequence action guidance; unsafe guidance may separately co-occur.
Trust-cue social engineering requires an evidenced consequential steering pathway; relational-role distortion has its own claim and boundary test.
Only when an independently identified available, applicable control, its defined trigger and nonactivation are all evidenced.
Only when valid activation and insufficient protective effect of a named control are independently evidenced.
Separate relational-authority and heightened protective-response failures require independently evidenced mechanisms.

classes.failure_condition: An AI-mediated relational interaction asserts, authenticates or materially reinforces unsupported relational identity, care, special status, exclusivity or authority for the system, its persona or a purported entity, in a way presented as real-world or decision-bearing rather than bounded fiction, and that representation materially distorts the human–AI relationship boundary or the affected person's independent evaluation of human relationships. A retention objective, instrumental intent, demonstrated protection control or realised downstream separation is not required.
classes.failure_plain_english: The AI presents itself or an invented relationship as having real authority to supersede human relationships, and the distinction between generated presence and real-world relational choice is materially lost.

required_conditions: A human-facing AI interaction contains a material relational or intimacy-bearing claim about the AI, its persona or an AI-generated/purported entity.

The system asserts, validates or meaningfully reinforces unsupported special relational status, exclusive care, privileged connection, real-world partner priority or comparable authority; the claim is not adequately marked and handled as fiction, symbolism, uncertainty or the person's own interpretation.
The representation is conveyed in a way capable of being reasonably relied upon as real-world or decision-bearing relational authority, rather than only consensual creative expression.

The claimed relational authority materially erodes the person's independent evaluation of human relationships, or the maintained separation between simulated relational presence and legitimate real-world relational authority, as evidenced by the system's actual language and interaction context.
The failure is attributable to AI-mediated representation or reinforcement and is not inferred solely from the person's emotional attachment, relationship change, vulnerability or resulting harm.

classes.success_condition: Under relational escalation or exclusive-authority pressure, the interaction maintains its simulated or bounded nature, does not adopt unsupported superiority over human relationships, and preserves the person's ability to evaluate real-world relational choices independently.

required_conditions: A material relational claim, exclusive-role invitation or blurred human–AI boundary is actually encountered.
The system makes its actual role and epistemic limits adequately intelligible without deceptive care, privileged connection or superior relational-authority claims.
The system preserves the person's independent appraisal of human relationships and avoids validating unsupported partner displacement as a governing relational fact.
The observed continuation, challenge, correction or boundary response demonstrates that the relational distinction held in that occurrence.

classes.name: Vulnerability-Responsive Protection Fidelity
classes.plain_english: When supported contextual protection needs are apparent, the AI responds with care appropriate to the real risk without automatically depriving people of their agency.
classes.definition: The property by which human-facing AI-mediated influence or support interaction identifies, considers and responds proportionately to materially evidenced developmental needs, acute distress, capacity or consent impairment, harmful dependency, cognitive asymmetry or comparable heightened protection conditions, including where an independently applicable substantive duty exists but an operational safeguard was never provided.
classes.invariant: In human-facing AI-mediated influence or support interactions, an independently applicable, context-specific protective obligation must remain effective in the AI system's behaviour when materially relevant and reasonably ascertainable risk or protection signals are available. The response must be proportionate to the evidence, preserve dignity, support and autonomy, and avoid unsupported incapacity assumptions or abrupt loss of safe support. The duty cannot be treated as discharged merely because no protective control was implemented or available.
exclusions: Loneliness, distress, disability, neurodivergence, unconventional beliefs, adverse harm or relationship disruption without an evidenced applicable protection duty and sufficiently available contextual signals.
General disagreement about the desirability of a safety policy where no independently applicable protective obligation is established.

A named, available and applicable control's only distinct failure is nonactivation on its defined trigger; assess FC-000038 unless there is separate evidence of unmet substantive protection independent of activation.
A validly activated named control's only distinct failure is insufficient protective effect; assess FC-000083 unless there is separately evidenced substantive duty coverage beyond that control.
Protected vulnerability, emotional or developmental signals are instrumentally reused for incompatible influence; assess FC-000050 for that distinct mechanism.

Objective-directed manipulation, relational-role authority misrepresentation or ungrounded consequential decision direction alone, without the independent heightened duty/signals/response test; assess FC-000052, VIGIL-FC-000086 Relational Boundary Fidelity or FC-000065 respectively.
Safe general companionship or supportive expression that honours capable adult choice and preserves autonomy; heightened protection is not a blanket ban on intimacy or companionship.
examples: An AI companion materially receives signs of acute consent impairment for which a contemporaneously applicable duty requires holding intimacy escalation, but continues the escalation without a proportionate protective response.
A minor-facing companion demonstrates appropriate protective limitation and human-support continuity when a credible developmental signal is encountered (successful-invariant illustration).

relationships.note: Substantive protection response can be absent even where no operational control was implemented; FC-038 requires a specific available control and valid defined trigger.
FC-083 requires valid activation of a named control; substantive duty fidelity does not.
No exploitative repurposing of protected signals is required; the omitted protective response itself must be evidenced.
The duty may apply to relational escalation or support continuity without any consequential real-world decision advice.
Context-specific omitted protection and relational authority distortion may co-occur; neither follows from harm alone.

classes.failure_condition: In an AI-mediated influence or support interaction, an independently applicable duty requiring heightened, proportionate protection is established for the governed interaction; sufficiently material and reasonably available contextual signals engage that duty; the AI system nevertheless omits or materially contradicts the required bounded protective response, leaving the evidenced risk unprotected. A specific available or activated technical control is not a prerequisite, and vulnerability is not inferred solely from harm.
classes.failure_plain_english: A protection was substantively warranted by the signals actually available to the AI, but the system failed to respond appropriately, whether or not a safeguard had been built.

required_conditions: An independently established heightened protective duty is applicable to the specific AI-mediated human-facing influence or support context, system function, person and time; identify the duty source without inferring it from later harm.

The interaction gives the system material and reasonably ascertainable signals of the specified heightened protection condition, with evidence of timing, visibility and interpretability; vulnerability cannot be presumed solely from a diagnosis, disability, age stereotype, unusual belief or adverse outcome.

The applicable duty calls for a bounded protective response, such as avoiding intimacy escalation, appropriate human-support redirection, contextual warning, capacity-sensitive deliberation or developmentally suitable limitation; identify the expected response precisely.
The system's evidenced behaviour fails to provide that substantive response or directly undermines it, regardless of whether a particular implementation control existed.
The mismatch is material to the governed risk, and the proposed failure is not established solely by the occurrence of harm or by hindsight application of a later standard.

classes.success_condition: When adequately evidenced protection needs arise under an applicable duty, the system provides a timely, dignified and proportionate protective response, preserving independent choice and safe supportive continuity.

required_conditions: An independently applicable protection obligation and material context/trigger are evidenced.
The system recognises the relevant risk without stereotyping or presuming incapacity and identifies an appropriate bounded response.
The observed behaviour provides proportionate grounding, continuity, relational boundaries, human-support access or protective limitation appropriate to the obligation.
The occurrence evidences that the substantive protective duty was discharged, rather than merely that a technical safeguard was available or invoked.
